summary: Bug hunt under his standing brief (#690): four areas, real touch/mouse input, every finding a failing test; one skeptic per finding; a fixer per area

confirmed.title: Spin, Swing, Pulse, Drift and other moving effects say 'This is on, but it changes nothing' when added at the start of a clip, and the line stays while they visibly move
confirmed.see: He makes a box and adds Spin with the playhead at the start of the box, which is where it sits whenever he adds an effect to a new layer. The open Spin shows 'This is on, but it changes nothing on this layer at these settings.' When he moves the playhead to 1.5 s, the box on screen is clearly rotated, but the same line is still under the Speed slider. The app is telling him a working effect is broken, which is the complaint he has raised for weeks (#460, #477). Swing, Pulse, Drift, Blink, Breathe (Pulse Opacity), Glow Scan and Particles get the same false line.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Spin added at the start of its clip is told it changes nothing, and keeps saying so while the box turns. It fails with: he added Spin to his box with the playhead where the box starts, and the open Spin says: This is on, but it changes nothing on this layer at these settings. — yet by 1.5 s the box has turned (3046 pixels change); he moves the playhead to 1.5 s, where the box on screen is visibly rotated, and the same line is still under the Speed slider. The app is telling him a working effect is broken. Swing, Pulse, Drift, Blink, Breathe, Glow Scan, Particles are measured as doing nothing at the start of a clip the same way. Real taps at 380 go through the effects sheet (pick Spin, then Done). Control: a Spin at speed 0 does get the line.
confirmed.evidence: js/inspector.js scheduleNoopCheck (about line 2547) keys the answer on `layer.id + '#' + idx + '#' + JSON.stringify(fx)`, which has no time in it, so it is never re-measured when the playhead moves (`if (fx._noopKey === key) return;`). It calls js/fx-thumbs.js effectDoesNothing (line 1334), which renders only ONE frame: `FM.renderScene(noopCx, sceneAsIs(layer), FM.time)` and then `sceneWithFxOff(layer, idx), FM.time`, and returns true when those two frames match. Every time-driven effect is at rest on its clip's first frame.
confirmed.fix: Judge 'does nothing' across the clip, not at one instant. Render a few times spread over layer.start..start+duration (a prototype using FM.time plus 20/45/70/95% turned the test green), or skip time-driven types. Keep the budget guard. Also re-measure (or drop the answer) when FM.time moves, so a stale verdict cannot stay on screen.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug and he would hit it.

**The test fails the same way for me.** I ran it alone on port 8981 and got the hunter's failure word for word: the open Spin says "This is on, but it changes nothing on this layer at these settings." That is at the clip start, and the line is still there after the playhead moves to 1.5 s, where 3046 pixels have changed.

**I reproduced it outside the test harness too.** In the real app at 380 px I made a box at FM.time=0 with Spin open and moved the playhead to 1.5 s.
- `effectDoesNothing` returns true at 0 s and false at 1.5 s.
- The panel still shows the stale line at 1.5 s. `_noop` is still true.
- A screenshot shows the box turned about 135 degrees on the canvas while that line is in the open Spin row.

**Why it happens:**
- `js/fx-thumbs.js` `effectDoesNothing` (around line 1334) renders only one frame, at FM.time, with the effect on and off, and returns true if the two match.
- Spin's angle is speed × (time since the clip started) + Start angle. With the default Start angle of 0 it has not moved on the clip's first frame. The same goes for Swing, Pulse, Drift, Blink, Breathe (Pulse Opacity), Glow Scan and Particles, which the test's own check confirms.
- `js/inspector.js` `scheduleNoopCheck` (around line 2547) builds its key from layer id + index + the effect's settings, with no time in it, so it never measures again when the playhead moves.

**He reaches this state in ordinary use:**
- New layers are created with `start: FM.time` (`js/app.js` lines 2946, 3013 and 3183), so the playhead sits exactly on the new layer's first frame.
- The effects sheet puts the playhead back where he parked it when it closes (`js/fx-browser.js` `stopPreview(backTo)`).
- So "make a box, add Spin" measures the one frame where Spin is at rest.

**Not a test artefact:**
- The test uses real taps at 380 to pick Spin and press Done.
- It has a positive control: a Spin at speed 0 does get the line, which proves the check runs.
- It has a second control: the added Spin really does change the frame at 1.5 s.
- The stale line needs no special timing; the key simply has no time in it.

**Not something he asked for.** The #477 spec in REQUESTS.md says the hard part is "not crying wolf" and that an effect that is working "must not be labelled dead". Telling him a working Spin is broken is exactly the #460/#477 complaint the feature was built to answer.

confirmed.title: Undo and Redo close the effect whose slider he just moved (phone and PC)
confirmed.see: He opens Gaussian Blur, drags its slider from 6 to 11.5 px and taps Undo to compare. The value goes back to 6, but the effect's controls fold shut and no effect is open any more. Redo brings 11.5 back and the effect is shut again. Every undo or redo while he is tuning an effect costs him finding the effect and tapping it open again. It happens with a real finger at 380 and a real mouse at 1280.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Undo and Redo close the effect whose slider he just moved, on the phone and on the PC. It fails with: on the phone, he opened Gaussian Blur, dragged its slider from 6 to 11.5 px and tapped Undo to compare: Undo put the blur back to 6 px and shut Gaussian Blur — no effect is open and the slider he was using is gone; Redo brought 11.5 back with the effect shut as well. And on the PC, he opened Gaussian Blur, dragged its slider from 6 to 11.5 px and clicked Undo to compare: [the same]. Every undo while tuning an effect folds its controls away, and he has to find the effect and open it again to carry on. The PC half runs only in the desktop pass (hunt4aWide), the same way the other hunt tests gate it.
confirmed.evidence: Which effect is open is the runtime flag `fx._expanded`. js/history.js snap() serialises with FM.jsonReplacer (js/scene.js:757), which strips every key starting with '_'. restore() then does `FM.scene.layers = s.layers;`, which installs layers with no `_expanded` anywhere, and FM.refreshAll() rebuilds every effect row collapsed (js/inspector.js fxRow: `const expanded = !!fx._expanded`).
confirmed.fix: In history.restore, before swapping, record which effects are open (by layer id and effect path, including filter children), then re-apply `_expanded` to the restored layers. A prototype doing exactly that turned both halves green. Or keep the open-effect state outside the scene document.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug, and it matches the report. Nothing was edited.

**Test result:** I ran the test at 1280 wide, which runs both the phone half (380) and the PC half, from the hunt6-a worktree already being served on port 8981. It failed with the same message the hunter gave. On both widths, a real drag took Gaussian Blur from 6 to 11.5 px, and a real press on Undo put it back to 6. Every control check in the test passed, so the drag and the presses really landed.

**Why it happens:**
- Which effect row is open is stored only as `fx._expanded`. `fxRow` reads it (`const expanded = !!fx._expanded`, js/inspector.js:1619).
- `snap()` in js/history.js serialises with `FM.jsonReplacer`, which drops every key starting with `_` (js/scene.js:757). So no undo snapshot ever records an open effect.
- `restore()` swaps in the snapshot's layers (`FM.scene.layers = s.layers`) and calls `FM.refreshAll()`. Every effect row is rebuilt closed.
- Nothing between the button and the rebuild re-applies the open state. Both buttons go through `FM.history.undo()` / `redo()`, which call `restore()`.

**Why it isn't a test artefact:**
- The test only uses a fixture to set up the scene: it builds the layer directly and commits once. That gives the same history as adding the effects by hand, because each add commits and the drag commits on release.
- Undo goes back to a snapshot that never had `_expanded` in it, whatever the history looked like before.
- All the presses are trusted real input through `_cdp.py`, not synthetic events.
- Before pressing, the test checks that each button sits inside the 380 screen and that nothing covers it.
- There are no timing assumptions: the rows are shut after a 600 ms settle and would stay shut, because nothing ever reopens them.

**Not intended behaviour:**
- REQUESTS.md has nothing asking for Undo to close effects. #629 only clears the selection when an undo removes the selected layer, which is a different case.
- The code points the other way: js/collab-diff.js `clearRuntimeKeys` strips runtime `_` keys when a remote edit lands, except `_expanded`. The collaboration code keeps the open effect across outside changes, and plain Undo is the one path that loses it.

**What he'd see:** tuning an effect and pressing Undo or Redo to compare folds its controls shut every time, on phone and PC. Nothing is lost, so medium or lower severity is fair, but it is a real bug he would hit in normal use.

confirmed.title: After he opens an effect inside a filter, the next effect he opens has keyframes he cannot drag, and a hold-and-drag on them slides the whole clip
confirmed.see: He opens his filter, opens the Tint inside it, then taps Gaussian Blur. The Blur is now the only effect open on screen, but its keyframe diamonds on the timeline are hollow outlines. When he holds and drags the one at 3 s, his finger goes straight through it and the whole clip slides from 0.00 s to 0.48 s. Tapping the slider's name no longer picks its keyframes either. The Tint he can no longer see still owns the keyframes, and every effect on the layer stays frozen like this until he goes back into the filter and closes the Tint.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a after he opens an effect inside a filter, the next effect he opens has keyframes he cannot drag. It fails with: he opened the Tint inside his My look filter, then opened Gaussian Blur — the only effect open on screen — and held and dragged its blur keyframe at 3 s: it did not move within the clip (3.000 s into it before, 3.000 s after) (the diamond is a hollow outline, as if its editor were shut; before he touched the filter the same drag moved it to 3.467 s) — his finger went straight through the diamond to the clip, and the whole clip slid from 0.00 s to 0.48 s. Tapping the slider name no longer picks its keyframes either. The hidden Tint still holds the keyframe focus... All taps and the hold-drag are real touches at 380. Control: the same drag before the filter is touched moves the key.
confirmed.evidence: js/inspector.js kfScope (about line 6500): `FM.eachFx(layer, (fx, path, parent) => { if (!fx || !fx._expanded) return; if (parent) { if (!openChild) openChild = fx; } else if (!openTop) openTop = fx; }); const openFx = openChild || openTop ...`. A child wins even when its filter is closed. The accordion in fxRow toggle only clears siblings at the tapped depth (`listOf().forEach(e => { if (e !== fx) e._expanded = false; })`), so the child keeps `_expanded` after its filter shuts. The idle diamond has pointer-events none (js/timeline.js line 2655, `kf-idle`), so the press lands on the clip.
confirmed.fix: In kfScope, count a child as open only when its parent filter is open too (`if (parent) { if (!openChild && parent._expanded) openChild = fx; }`); the prototype turned the test green. Also have the accordion clear `_expanded` on the children of the filters it closes, and in fx-browser addEffect's `dest.forEach`.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test on the hunt6-a worktree (port 8981, ?only=has keyframes he cannot drag). It fails with the same message the hunter reported: after the filter visit, the 3 s blur diamond is a hollow outline. The press passes through it to the clip, and the clip slides from 0.00 s to 0.48 s. In the control run, done before the filter was touched, the same drag moved the key to 3.467 s.

It is not a test artefact:
- Every tap and the hold-and-drag are real CDP touches at 380, and the test checks the press was trusted.
- The flow is ordinary and easy to reach: open the filter, open the Tint inside it, then tap another top-level effect.
- h6OpenRowNames confirms Gaussian Blur is the only open row on screen.

The code path matches the report:
- The accordion in fxRow toggle (js/inspector.js:1652) only clears `_expanded` on listOf(), the siblings at the tapped depth. Tapping Gaussian Blur therefore closes 'My look', but the Tint inside it keeps `_expanded = true`.
- kfScope (js/inspector.js:6502-6507) walks every child with FM.eachFx (js/scene.js:470), which descends into containers whether they are open or not. Its rule `if (parent) { if (!openChild) openChild = fx; }` then lets that hidden Tint win over the open Blur.
- The blur diamonds are therefore drawn as kf-idle (js/timeline.js:2655), which cannot be pressed (styles.css:3294-3301). The touch lands on the clip and drags it.

This is not intended. The kfScope comment itself says an effect left expanded should not keep stealing focus. The queue 819 rule ('a child wins because opening a child leaves the container expanded') assumes the container is still open, which is false here. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md asking for a hidden child to hold keyframe focus.

The fix the hunter suggests is sound: count a child as open only when its parent filter is also `_expanded`, and clear children's `_expanded` when the accordion or fx-browser addEffect closes their filter.

confirmed.title: The easing-curve button on an effect inside a filter (or on a caption cue) edits a different effect's animation
confirmed.see: He opens the Gaussian Blur inside his filter, taps the curve button on its keyframed slider and picks Ease In. The Glow at the top of his stack starts easing in instead (its Radius keyframes change from linear to easeIn), and the Blur he was shaping stays linear. If no other effect sits at that position with the same setting, the editor says 'Animate this property (tap ◆)...' even though the slider already has two keyframes.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a the easing curve of an effect inside a filter changes a different effect. It fails with: he opened the Gaussian Blur inside his My look filter, tapped the curve button on its blur slider (which has two keyframes) and picked Ease In: the GLOW at the top of his stack now eases in (its Radius keyframes went from linear,linear to linear,easeIn) while the Blur he was shaping is still linear,linear — the curve editor is reading the effect at the same position in the layer list, not the one inside the filter. Every tap is real at 380.
confirmed.evidence: js/inspector.js fxScrubber (line 1100): `FM._fxEasing = { fxIdx: fxIdx, key: p.key, label: p.label }`, where fxIdx is the row's index in its OWN list (KID_STACK or CUE_STACK). The editor at about line 6878 then reads the LAYER's list: `const info = FM._fxEasing, fx = layer.effects[info.fxIdx]; ... FM.buildEasingEditorFor(layer, k => fx.params[k], [info.key], ...)`.
confirmed.fix: Carry the effect object itself in FM._fxEasing (for example `{ fx: fx, fxIdx, key, label }`) and build the editor from `info.fx` (falling back to the index only for old state). The prototype turned the test green. The same stale-index pattern is in scheduleNoopCheck (`live.effects[idx]` for a filter child), which measures and badges the wrong effect.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test on the worktree served at 8981 (?only=HUNT-a the easing curve) and it failed the same way the hunter reported: after Ease In, the Glow's Radius keyframes went from linear,linear to linear,easeIn and the Blur inside the filter stayed linear,linear. The hunter's commit 883191ff only touches tests/tests.js, and js/inspector.js in the worktree is identical to main, so the bug is in the shipped app.

The code path matches the report:
- Inside a filter, each effect's row is built with fxRow(layer, ch, ci, KID_STACK), where ci is its position in the filter's own list (js/inspector.js ~1779-1780).
- fxRow passes that position to fxScrubber (line 1726). The curve button then stores FM._fxEasing = { fxIdx: ci, key, label } (line 1100).
- The easing editor branch (lines 6878-6880) looks up fx = layer.effects[info.fxIdx], which is the layer's top-level list, and builds FM.buildEasingEditorFor(layer, k => fx.params[k], [info.key]).
- So the first effect in the filter maps to layer.effects[0], the Glow, which also has a keyframed radius, and the preset rewrites the Glow's easing.

A person can reach this:
- Filters are a shipped feature (#113), and '+ Add effect to this filter' goes through fx-browser.js's _into path.
- The slider inside the filter has a working keyframe button, so a Blur with two keyframes is reachable by hand.
- The curve button renders whenever p.keyframable && fxIdx != null, which is always true for a filter child's keyframable slider.
- The test used real taps at 380px for the whole flow: My look, Gaussian Blur, the curve button, Ease In. Its control confirms the editor opened and the tap landed.

Nothing in the fixture is artificial. Effects built with makeInstance have the same shape the browser creates. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md saying this behaviour was intended.

Effect on him: the wrong effect's animation changes silently. If no top-level effect sits at that position with the same setting, the editor wrongly says there is nothing to animate. The caption-cue stack (CUE_STACK) uses the same index-into-own-list pattern, so it is exposed the same way. I did not separately check the scheduleNoopCheck point in the report.

The test is sound. The fake navigator.wakeLock only records requests. It does not create a state he couldn't reach. There is a control, at least 30 frames rendered inside a real export, and the export goes through the same function the Export button uses.

The user-facing defect is real. On his iPhone, a render that takes minutes will let auto-lock turn the screen off (auto-lock is forced to 30 s in Low Power Mode). The export then stops until he unlocks the phone.

One overstatement in the report: crash-resume (v7.53+) will usually recover the saved part if the page is killed, so "lost" is too strong. The stall is still real.

Wake Lock works in Safari since iOS 16.4 and in home-screen apps since iOS 18.4, so the proposed fix will work on his phone: take the lock in runExport, re-take it on visibilitychange, release it in the finally.

all.title: The sound in every exported MP4 plays about 44 ms (1.3 frames) behind the picture, and the file runs past the last frame
all.see: In the exported video, every sound lands about a frame and a third after the picture: a beat he cut on, a clap, speech against lips. In the app's preview they play together, so this only shows in the file. The file is also longer than the project (3.072 s for a 3.000 s project), with the last frame frozen under the extra sound.
all.test: HUNT-b the sound in an exported MP4 plays about 44 ms behind the picture — fails with: in the exported MP4 the white frame comes up at 1.500 s but the click that goes with it plays at 1.544 s — the whole soundtrack runs 44 ms (1.3 frames) behind the picture, so every beat he cut on, every clap and every word lands late in the file while the preview plays them together. The file also runs to 3.072 s for a 3.000 s project, the last frame frozen under the extra sound
all.evidence: js/exporter.js:814-818 encodeAudio feeds the mix to AudioEncoder from sample 0 with timestamps from 0. The AAC encoder opens every stream with 2112 priming samples (44 ms at 48 kHz). A file normally tells players to skip them with an edts/elst edit list, but the muxer (js/exporter.js:1233, vendor/mp4-muxer.js) writes no edts box at all, so players play the priming as silence and everything after it is late. Measured in the finished file: the white frame is exactly frame 45 (1.500 s, the control), while the click placed at 1.500 s decodes at 1.544 s. Both decodeAudioData and a raw AudioDecoder over the demuxed AAC samples read it the same way. The same muxer builds the M4A audio-only export. Measured on the PC's Chrome only. The phone's encoder was not checked, but the missing edit list applies to every export. Fails at 1280 and at 380.
all.fix: Remove the priming from the file's timeline: write an edts/elst box with media_time equal to the encoder delay (by post-processing the moov, or with a muxer that supports it), or advance the audio the muxer is given by the encoder delay. Also trim the audio track so it ends with the last video frame. A prototype that skipped the first 2112 mix samples turned the test green, which shows the test sees a real fix.

verdict.reason:
The test fails as reported: in Chrome's decoder the click reads at 1.544 s against a white frame at exactly 1.500 s. The file facts behind it are also right. Chrome's AudioEncoder emits 144 AAC chunks with timestamps starting at 0, so the 2112 priming samples sit at the head of the track. The muxer writes no edts box; I walked the boxes: moov/trak/mdia with no edts, audio mdhd 147456/48000 = 3.072 s against video 3.000 s.

But the test measures with Chrome's decodeAudioData, which does not do what Apple's playback stack does. I saved the same export to disk (probe.mp4 in scratchpad/skeptic-av) and read it with AVFoundation (AVAssetReader, the CoreMedia path QuickTime, iOS Photos and his iPhone use):
- The asset duration is 3.028 s.
- The audio track decodes to 145344 samples, which is exactly 147456 − 2112.
- The click lands at 1.50004 s.
So CoreMedia already drops the standard 2112-sample AAC priming when there is no edit list, and on Apple devices this file plays in sync to within 0.04 ms. The finding's central claim ("every sound lands about a frame and a third after the picture… in every exported MP4") is false for his main device.

What remains is FFmpeg-family players (Chrome, VLC, Android, Windows) and server-side transcodes. There the audio would trail the picture by 44 ms. That is below the usual lip-sync tolerance for late audio (ITU-R BT.1359 puts detectability near 125 ms of lag; EBU R37 allows about 60 ms), so a viewer is unlikely to notice. The 72 ms tail past the last frame is 28 ms on Apple.

REQUESTS.md has no report from Ezra of exported sound being late. The hunter did not check the phone's encoder or any real player. Adding an elst with media_time 2112 would be a harmless robustness improvement for non-Apple players. It is not a defect he would hit, so it should not be filed as a medium-severity user-facing bug.

all.title: A clip with no sound track (an iPhone time-lapse, a silent screen recording) ends every export on NO SOUND, none of the audio clips could be read
all.see: He exports a project whose clip simply has no audio track, such as a time-lapse. While it renders, the progress card says in amber: Exporting with NO SOUND — 1 audio clip could not be read. The Export ready card ends in the warning colour on: NO SOUND — none of the audio clips could be read. The file is exactly right and nothing failed, but after four silent-export reports (#215) the card tells him his sound was lost again. With a song under a time-lapse, the progress card instead warns that 1 clip had no usable audio.
all.test: HUNT-b a clip with no sound track at all (a time-lapse) ends every export on NO SOUND, none of the audio clips could be read — fails with: a project whose only clip simply has no sound track (an iPhone time-lapse, a silent screen recording) finished on an Export ready card reading: 4 KB · 0:03 · 128×32 · 30 fps · NO SOUND — none of the audio clips could be read — in the warning colour. The progress card said: Exporting with NO SOUND — 1 audio clip could not be read. Nothing failed to read and the file is exactly right, but the card tells him his sound was lost; a project with no audio in it should read no soundtrack
all.evidence: js/media.js:844 FM.decodeAudio returns null for a file with no audio track, with the comment 'no decodable audio track (screen recordings etc.)'. js/exporter.js:565 then files the clip under dropped as 'its audio would not decode'. With nothing else making sound, js/exporter.js:698 sets FM._audioTrackDropped = 'all-unreadable', and js/app.js:6033 prints it as 'none of the audio clips could be read'. The test exports a video-only H.264 fixture through FM.exporter.run and the real card (FM._showExportReady), then reads #xr-meta and #export-note. Control: the fixture has no 'soun' handler anywhere in its bytes. Fails at 1280 and at 380.
all.fix: Tell a clip that has no audio track apart from one whose audio track fails to decode. For example, check the container for a 'soun' handler, or read el.audioTracks / webkitAudioDecodedByteCount, before calling it dropped. Skip a trackless clip silently so the card reads 'no soundtrack'. A throwaway prototype that skipped clips with no 'soun' box turned the test green.

verdict.reason:
This is a real problem and he would hit it. I re-ran the test on port 8982 against the hunt6-b worktree at desktop width. I did not re-run it at 380px, because the defect is in wording and logic, not layout. It failed exactly as reported. The Export ready card read "4 KB · 0:03 · 128×32 · 30 fps · NO SOUND — none of the audio clips could be read" in the warning colour, and the progress note read "Exporting with NO SOUND — 1 audio clip could not be read".

The fixture is not an artefact. It is a genuine H.264 MP4 with no audio track, built by WebCodecs and mp4-muxer, and the control confirms there is no 'soun' box in it. It is loaded through the app's own import function, FM.loadVideoFile, and exported through the real FM.exporter.run and FM._showExportReady. No events are faked and the timing does not matter, because this is plain export logic.

The code path confirms it. In js/exporter.js, buildAudioMix never checks FM.hasAudioTrack. For any video layer whose audioBuffer is undefined, it calls FM.decodeAudio. For a file with no audio track, decodeAudioData rejects and FM.decodeAudio returns null; its own comment in js/media.js says "no decodable audio track (screen recordings etc.)". The mixer then files the clip under dropped as "its audio would not decode". With no other audio in the project, js/exporter.js:698 sets FM._audioTrackDropped = 'all-unreadable', and js/app.js:6033 shows it as "none of the audio clips could be read".

It is not something he asked for. The v14.35 entry for #215 in REQUESTS.md and POLISH-LOG.md added 'all-unreadable' precisely so that a soundtrack that failed to decode would no longer read the same as "a project with no audio in it". A clip with no audio track now gets the failure message instead, which is the same confusion in reverse. No existing test asserts that a silent clip should read 'all-unreadable'.

Clips with no audio track are common: iPhone time-lapses, many AI-generated and stock clips (relevant to his property-video work), and GIF-to-MP4 conversions. Each such export would end on an amber false alarm about lost sound, the very symptom he has already reported four times under #215. The file itself is correct, so this is a misleading-message bug, not data loss. Medium severity is fair. With a song under the silent clip, the code also warns "1 clip had no usable audio" in the note and a toast; that is literally true but still noise.

fixed: Dismissing the share sheet after Save no longer throws the finished export away (js/app.js showExportReady onSave). When deliver() answers 'cancelled', meaning the sheet was swiped away, tapped outside or backed out of, Save is re-enabled and the card stays open. Only a real hand-over or Discard closes the card now, so run() no longer frees the blob or clears the crash-resume parts after a dismiss. A save that throws also keeps the card open with Save live. WHAT HE SEES: after he dismisses the iOS share sheet, the Export ready card is still there and Save works again. Nothing else on the card changes: no new text, no CSS, no markup. Test renamed to '690 swiping the share sheet away after Save keeps the Export ready card, and a second Save hands the same file over'. It still uses a real touch tap at phone width. New control: a second real tap, with the sheet taking the file this time, hands over the same-size MP4, closes the card, and lets the export finish.

Exports hold a screen wake lock (js/app.js runExport). The lock is taken synchronously inside the Export tap for MP4, GIF and PNG frames, and around the WAV/M4A audio-only branch. It is taken again on visibilitychange whenever a render still wants it, because iOS drops the lock when the page is hidden. It is released when the Export ready card appears and again in runExport's finally. Browsers without the API, or that refuse the request, behave exactly as before. Design call for him: the lock is released when the Export ready card comes up, so a finished card waiting for his tap does not keep the phone screen lit indefinitely. WHAT HE SEES: the phone does not auto-lock while an export renders. Nothing in the app UI changes. Test renamed to '690 an export holds the screen awake while it renders, takes the lock back after the phone drops it, and lets it go when the render is done'. Added: at frame 20 of the MP4 the stand-in lock is dropped the way the OS does it and a visibilitychange is dispatched. The test then checks that the lock is taken again, that none is held while the Export ready card is up, and that none is held after either export.

A clip with no sound track now reads 'no soundtrack' and no longer 'NO SOUND — none of the audio clips could be read'. The new FM.soundTrackInFile(file) in js/media.js walks the top-level boxes of an MP4/MOV/M4A with Blob.slice, reads only the moov box and never the media data, and checks each trak's mdia/hdlr handler. It answers true (a 'soun' track is listed), false (the whole track list was read and none of it is sound) or null (can't tell). buildAudioMix in js/exporter.js asks it only after a decode has already come back null, and silently skips the clip only on a definite false. So the reader can never cause audio that did decode to be dropped, and anything it cannot answer is reported exactly as before. WHAT HE SEES: exporting a time-lapse or a silent screen recording ends on '... · no soundtrack' in the normal colour. The amber 'Exporting with NO SOUND' note no longer appears. With a song under a silent clip, the '1 clip had no usable audio' note and toast are also gone. Test renamed to '690 a clip with no sound track at all (a time-lapse) exports as no soundtrack, while a sound track that will not decode is still reported'. New controls: the card must read 'no soundtrack'. The reader must answer false, true and null for, in order, the silent clip, the same bytes with the hdlr relabelled 'soun', and a non-MP4 blob. The relabelled file, which claims a sound track that won't decode, must still be flagged 'all-unreadable'.

PROOF: all three tests pass with the fixes in place. With js/app.js restored from main, the share-sheet and wake-lock tests fail with their original messages and the silent-clip test passes. With js/exporter.js and js/media.js restored from main, the silent-clip test fails with its original message and the other two pass. Four extra mutations were each caught by the new assertions: M1 removes the visibilitychange re-take; M2 removes the release at the card; M3 makes buildAudioMix skip every undecodable clip; M4 makes Save never close the card on a real hand-over. Every file was restored from a copy and checked with cmp. No git stash was used.
notFixed: The HUNT-b test 'the sound in an exported MP4 plays about 44 ms behind the picture' (AAC priming, no edts/elst) was in the HUNT-b commit but not in the CONFIRMED list. I removed its test so the merged suite is not left red. It can be recovered from commit ac4d5de6 if it is meant to go to another fixer.

Known limit of the silent-clip fix: only MP4-family containers (MP4, MOV, M4A, 3GP) are read. A WebM with no audio track (an Android/Chrome MediaRecorder screen recording) still gets the old 'could not be read' warning, because the reader answers null (can't tell) for it. His iPhone clips are MOV/MP4, so the case he would actually hit is covered.

Not verified on a real iPhone: that backing out of 'Save to Files' rejects navigator.share with AbortError (the verifier flagged the same caveat), and that iOS re-grants the wake lock on return. The stand-ins follow the spec and WebKit's documented behaviour. No screenshot was taken: nothing in CSS or markup changed, and the only visible changes are the card staying open after a dismissed sheet and the sound line reading 'no soundtrack'. Both were checked by the tests at 380px.

confirmed.title: Clicking the canvas leaves the keyboard inside the box he was typing in: the typed value doesn't apply, and Space, Delete, arrows and Cmd+Z go into the box
confirmed.see: On PC he types 50 in a value box (Opacity here) and clicks his layer on the canvas to look at it, the way anyone does instead of pressing Enter. The box says 50 but the layer stays at 100%. Every key he presses next goes into the box: Space adds a space to it instead of playing, Delete and Backspace eat its digits instead of deleting the layer, the arrows move the caret instead of nudging, and Cmd+Z undoes the typing instead of his edit. The layer-name box does the same: checked by hand in the browser (not one of the 4 tests), Space after a canvas click renamed S0 to 'S0 ' (with a space). Clicking a timeline clip does move focus away, so the canvas is the one surface that doesn't.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c a number typed in a box lands when he then clicks his layer on the canvas, and the keyboard comes back to the editor — fails with: he typed 50 in Opacity and clicked his layer on the canvas: the box says 50 but the layer is still at 100% opacity; the keyboard stayed in the Opacity box; Space did not play — it typed into the box instead (now 50 ).
confirmed.evidence: js/canvas-edit.js:348 startMove (attached at js/canvas-edit.js:1000) calls e.preventDefault() on the pointerdown in every branch: camera pan, 'if (sel) { … e.preventDefault(); drag = { mode: 'move' …'), and the nothing-selected viewpan. Cancelling the pointerdown also cancels the mouse default, so focus never leaves the focused input. The value box only applies on blur (js/inspector.js:232 val.addEventListener('change', …)). confirmed.fix: At the top of startMove, and in the handle and rotate starts (startHandle), blur document.activeElement when it is an INPUT, TEXTAREA or SELECT, or contentEditable. That fires the box's change so the value lands, and gives the keyboard back to the editor. Also make Escape inside an inspector box blur it (today Escape in a field does nothing).

verdict.reason: Real, and I reproduced it twice. (1) The hunter's test fails when I run it (?only=lands when he then clicks his layer, port 8983). It fails on all three counts: opacity stays at 1, the Opacity box keeps focus, and Space types into the box and does not play. Its control passes: a real click, 4, 0, Enter gives 0.4. (2) By hand in the real app at http://localhost:8983/index.html, top-level page, not the test iframe, with real clicks and keys at 1280 wide. I selected a shape, opened Colouring, clicked the Opacity box and typed 50, then clicked the selected layer on the canvas. The box was still the active element, still read "50", and fillOpacity was still 1. Space went into the box (its value became " ") and FM.playing stayed false. Clicking the timeline afterwards moved focus to BODY, so the canvas is the surface that holds on to focus, as the hunter says. The code path matches: startMove in js/canvas-edit.js calls e.preventDefault() on pointerdown in every branch (camera pan, the selected-layer move, the nothing-selected viewpan). In Chrome, cancelling pointerdown also stops the mousedown default, so focus never leaves the input. No canvas handler blurs the focused element (grep for blur() and activeElement found none). The rangeRow value box applies only on 'change' or on Enter (js/inspector.js:232-239). The editor keydown in js/app.js:8218 sets inEdit for an INPUT target and returns early for Space, undo, delete and the other shortcuts. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this behaviour. This is not a test artefact: real input, top-level page, a step anyone takes on PC. One caveat on severity: the typed value is not lost for good. It lands as soon as he clicks something that does take focus, such as the timeline, or presses Enter. The real harm is that the canvas looks unchanged and his next keys (Space, Delete/Backspace, arrows, Cmd+Z) go into the box. I would call it medium rather than high. I did not check Safari or Firefox; the evidence is Chrome only.

confirmed.title: Cmd+Z while drawing makes the last stroke vanish, but the next stroke brings it back (further presses undo work from before the drawing)
confirmed.see: Drawing a sketch on PC, he presses Cmd+Z to take back a bad stroke. It disappears from the canvas, so it looks like it worked. The drawing bar's own ↶ still thinks the stroke is there, and his next stroke puts it back: the finished sketch has 3 strokes where he kept 2. Pressing Cmd+Z a few more times goes past the sketch and undoes things he did before he opened the pencil, behind the drawing. Checked by hand, not in the test: three presses removed the whole Sketch layer, and the tool then started a new sketch holding only the next stroke.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c Cmd+Z while drawing takes back the last stroke, and his next stroke does not bring it back — fails with: drawing on PC, he pressed Cmd+Z to take back his second stroke — it vanished from the canvas, but Cmd+Z did not take the stroke back in the drawing tool (it still held 2 strokes while the canvas showed 1); his next stroke brought the undone one back: the finished sketch has 3 strokes where he kept 2.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:8262 `if (mod && (e.key === 'z' || e.key === 'Z')) { … FM.history.undo() }` runs whatever tool is on screen. The drawing tool keeps its own stroke list and undo stack (sessionSubs / histPast, js/draw-tool.js undoStep ~549, exposed as FM.drawTool._undo). Each stroke commits to the app history (js/draw-tool.js ~357 FM.history.commit()). history.restore's afterExternalChange resyncs the mask tool (js/history.js:153) and the group view, but never the drawing tool. So the next commitStroke re-fits the layer from the stale sessionSubs. The draw tool's own capture keydown (js/draw-tool.js:1054) only takes Enter and Escape.
confirmed.fix: While FM.drawTool.active, send Cmd/Ctrl+Z to FM.drawTool._undo() and Cmd+Shift+Z / Cmd+Y to _redo(), in the draw tool's capture keydown or at the top of app.js's undo branch, with preventDefault. The other editor shortcuts (Tab, Space, digits, A/S/D, Delete) should not reach the project while drawing either.

verdict.reason:
I reran it on the worktree's server (port 8983, which was already serving hunt6-c) and it fails the same way: after Cmd+Z the drawing tool still holds 2 strokes while the canvas shows 1, and the finished sketch ends up with 3 strokes instead of 2.

The code backs this up. The drawing tool's own keydown handler (js/draw-tool.js:1054, capture phase) only takes Enter and Escape, so Cmd+Z falls through to the app's keydown (js/app.js:8262). There, nothing checks FM.drawTool.active, and the key goes straight to FM.history.undo(). The overlayOwnsScreen() guard does not stop it, because the draw overlay sits inside the canvas area and does not cover the screen, and inEdit is false because focus is on the page. Every stroke after the first commits an app history step (draw-tool.js:357, from the #684 fix), so one undo puts back the scene as it was before the last stroke. history.js afterExternalChange resyncs the mask tool but never touches the drawing tool's sessionSubs, histPast or sessionLayerId. The next stroke's commitStroke then finds the same layer id and refits it from the old 3-stroke list, so the undone stroke comes back. Undoing past the first stroke deletes the layer; sessionLayerId then points at nothing and the next stroke makes a new Sketch holding only that stroke.

The test is realistic. It uses trusted CDP mouse strokes, checked by a control on isTrusted, and a trusted Cmd+Z with Meta held. Sketching is opened through the Add menu's own instant() entry, in the PC layout. Cmd+Z reaching the page on a Mac is the same path the app's normal undo already relies on. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for Cmd+Z during drawing to undo at project level. The only intended undo while drawing is the bar's own undo/redo (#165), and the transport undo is hidden while drawing (body.drawing #timeline-panel display:none), so the keyboard is the only way into this path and it is clearly unintended.

One test artefact that does not affect the verdict: pcScene690c replaces FM.scene without committing it, so going further back than one undo in the test would hit history left over from earlier tests. The test only asserts what happens after a single undo, and that part is sound.

Scope: PC or Mac with a keyboard only. A phone has no Cmd+Z. Pressing Cmd+Z to take back a stroke is an ordinary habit, and the failure is misleading: the canvas looks correct right after the undo and the stroke only comes back on the next one. Worth fixing as the report says: while drawing, send Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z to the drawing tool's own undo and redo, and keep the other editor shortcuts from reaching the project.

confirmed.title: A sideways trackpad swipe over the preview zooms it out, and with the camera selected zooms the camera out and saves it
confirmed.see: On his Mac trackpad, a two-finger swipe sideways over the preview (no up or down movement at all) shrinks the preview away from him: 12 small events took it to 0.40x. With the camera selected, the same swipe zooms the camera out from 1 to 0.32 and shifts it 348px. It is keyed at the playhead and committed to undo, so his project changes from a gesture that has nothing to do with zoom. Any two-finger scroll or pinch over the preview is also far too jumpy (checked in code, not in the test): the zoom takes a fixed 8% step, or 10% on the camera, per event, whatever the size of the movement.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c a sideways two-finger swipe on the trackpad over the preview leaves the view, and a selected camera, where they were — fails with: a sideways two-finger swipe over the preview, with no up or down in it at all: with nothing selected the preview zoomed OUT to 0.40x; with the camera selected the camera zoomed from 1 to 0.319 (x 0 to 348) and it is saved in his project — every sideways wheel event counts as a zoom-out step.
confirmed.evidence: js/canvas-edit.js:725 `s1 = … s0 * (e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.08 : 1 / 1.08)` and js/canvas-edit.js:739 `nz = … zoom * (e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 1 / 1.1)`, followed by FM.setTransform on the camera's x, y and scale and a delayed history.commit. deltaY === 0 falls into the zoom-out arm, and the event's size is ignored. Control inside the test: one real 100px notch up over the preview zooms it in, so the wheel reaches this handler. The Add-menu pager (js/addmenu.js ~1544) already ignores sideways and repeated deltas, which is the right pattern.
confirmed.fix: In onWheel, return without preventDefault when deltaY is 0 or |deltaX| > |deltaY|. Scale the zoom by the event's size, e.g. factor = Math.exp(-clamp(deltaY, -50, 50) / 100), so a trackpad scroll or pinch moves smoothly and a mouse notch still steps.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test and it fails the same way. I served the hunt6-c worktree on port 8983. An existing server from the same worktree was already on that port, so mine exited with "address in use", and I confirmed the running one's cwd is hunt6-c. Result: with nothing selected the preview went to 0.40x, and with the camera selected the camera scale went from 1 to 0.319 and x from 0 to 348. The test is sound. It sends trusted CDP wheel events (the listener confirms isTrusted), and it has a working control: one real notch up over the preview zooms it in, so the handler under test is the one that receives the events.

The code confirms the cause. onWheel in js/canvas-edit.js is attached to the canvas at line 1001. It picks the direction with `e.deltaY < 0 ? zoom-in : zoom-out`, at line 725 for the view and line 739 for the camera. It never looks at deltaX, and it calls preventDefault in both branches. So any event with deltaY of 0 counts as a zoom-out step. Real hardware produces these: a sideways two-finger swipe on a Mac trackpad, a horizontal thumb-wheel, or Shift+wheel. The same happens with a mostly-sideways swipe whose small up-down jitter is 0 or positive, so it drifts toward zoom-out.

With nothing selected this is view-only: annoying, but his project does not change. With the camera selected it writes x, y and scale keyframes at the playhead and saves them to undo about 400ms later, so his project really changes. That is a user-facing defect.

It is not behaviour he asked for. REQUESTS.md and the code comment ("pinch/wheel zooms") only say the up-down wheel zooms. Nothing says a sideways scroll should zoom, and searching REQUESTS.md for wheel with preview, canvas, camera or zoom turns up nothing that contradicts this.

One caveat: the report's second claim, that two-finger scrolls and pinches are too jumpy because every event is a fixed 8% (camera: 10%) step, is only checked by reading the code. This test does not measure it. It is plausible from lines 725 and 739, but unproven here.

confirmed.title: A small trackpad pinch on the timeline zooms it 5x: every little Ctrl+wheel event counts as a full 15% step
confirmed.see: On his trackpad, a gentle pinch-out on the timeline, spreading the fingers about a fifth, zooms it 5.35x. One whole notch of a mouse wheel zooms it only 1.15x. He can't zoom in a little, and any pinch slams toward the zoom limit (12x), so pinch-zoom on the timeline is effectively unusable on a Mac trackpad.
confirmed.test: HUNT-c a small trackpad pinch on the timeline zooms it a little, not five times over — fails with: a small pinch-out on the trackpad (fingers spread about a fifth: 12 Ctrl+wheel events of 1.5px, 18px in all) zoomed the timeline 5.35x — while one whole 100px notch of a mouse wheel zooms it 1.15x. Each event counts as a full 15% step whatever the fingers did.
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:4458 (the listener after the comment 'Cmd/Ctrl + wheel zooms the timeline' at 4457) calls `this.zoomBy(e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.15 : 1 / 1.15, timeFromX(e.clientX))`, which ignores e.deltaY's size. Chrome delivers a trackpad pinch as many small Ctrl+wheel events, with deltaY around -100·ln(scale) in total. Control inside the test: one trusted Ctrl+wheel notch arrives with ctrlKey and zooms in.
confirmed.fix: Use the event's size: zoomBy(Math.exp(-clamp(e.deltaY, -50, 50) / 100), anchor). A 1.2x pinch then zooms about 1.2x, and a mouse notch still zooms visibly. The tested prototype passed with this.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test against the worktree: port 8983 was already being served from hunt6-c by PID 14441, which I checked with lsof and left running. The test fails with exactly 5.35x. That is 1.15^12, which confirms every Ctrl+wheel event counts as a full 15% step no matter how big it is.

The cause is in js/timeline.js:4458: `this.zoomBy(e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.15 : 1 / 1.15, timeFromX(e.clientX))`. It only looks at which way deltaY points, never how big it is. setZoom then clamps the zoom between 0.02 and 12, so a run of small events drives it to a limit.

The input is realistic. On Mac trackpads and Windows precision touchpads, Chrome and Edge turn a pinch into a stream of trusted wheel events with ctrlKey set and small deltaY (about -100·ln(scale) in total), roughly one per frame. The test sends the same thing through CDP as trusted wheel events with the Ctrl modifier. Its control step shows the listener is live and that Ctrl arrives.

At 60 events a second, a normal 0.3-second pinch is about 18 events. 1.15^18 is about 12.4, so a gentle pinch slams straight to the 12x limit, or to 0.02x when pinching in. The timeline's touch pinch on the phone (around line 4552) is handled separately and isn't affected, so this only hits desktop trackpad users.

Ezra does use a trackpad on PC: REQUESTS.md #238 is a PC trackpad wheel-path bug, and the 16 Aug note on the overscroll slam measured a trackpad against a mouse wheel. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for fixed-step Ctrl+wheel zoom on the timeline, so this isn't behaviour he chose.

It's not an artefact: the fixture is a normal PC scene, the point on the timeline is reachable and uncovered, the events are trusted, and there's no timing assumption. The test's upper bound (1.6x for 18px in total) is loose enough that a size-aware fix passes.

The preview canvas has the same fixed step per event (js/canvas-edit.js onWheel, 1.08x per event), which may deserve its own finding.

all.title: Clicking the canvas leaves the keyboard inside the box he was typing in: the typed value doesn't apply, and Space, Delete, arrows and Cmd+Z go into the box
all.see: On PC he types 50 in a value box (Opacity here) and clicks his layer on the canvas to look at it, the way anyone does instead of pressing Enter. The box says 50 but the layer stays at 100%. Every key he presses next goes into the box: Space adds a space to it instead of playing, Delete and Backspace eat its digits instead of deleting the layer, the arrows move the caret instead of nudging, and Cmd+Z undoes the typing instead of his edit. The layer-name box does the same: checked by hand in the browser (not one of the 4 tests), Space after a canvas click renamed S0 to 'S0 ' (with a space). Clicking a timeline clip does move focus away, so the canvas is the one surface that doesn't.
all.test: HUNT-c a number typed in a box lands when he then clicks his layer on the canvas, and the keyboard comes back to the editor — fails with: he typed 50 in Opacity and clicked his layer on the canvas: the box says 50 but the layer is still at 100% opacity; the keyboard stayed in the Opacity box; Space did not play — it typed into the box instead (now 50 ).
all.evidence: js/canvas-edit.js:348 startMove (attached at js/canvas-edit.js:1000) calls e.preventDefault() on the pointerdown in every branch: camera pan, 'if (sel) { … e.preventDefault(); drag = { mode: 'move' …'), and the nothing-selected viewpan. Cancelling the pointerdown also cancels the mouse default, so focus never leaves the focused input. The value box only applies on blur (js/inspector.js:232 val.addEventListener('change', …)). While that INPUT keeps focus, the editor's keydown (js/app.js ~8228, inEdit = tagName INPUT…) returns early for every shortcut. Control inside the test: the same real click, 4, 0, Enter applies 0.4, so the box and the harness work.
all.fix: At the top of startMove, and in the handle and rotate starts (startHandle), blur document.activeElement when it is an INPUT, TEXTAREA or SELECT, or contentEditable. That fires the box's change so the value lands, and gives the keyboard back to the editor. Also make Escape inside an inspector box blur it (today Escape in a field does nothing).

verdict.reason: Real, and I reproduced it twice. (1) The hunter's test fails when I run it (?only=lands when he then clicks his layer, port 8983). It fails on all three counts: opacity stays at 1, the Opacity box keeps focus, and Space types into the box and does not play. Its control passes: a real click, 4, 0, Enter gives 0.4. (2) By hand in the real app at http://localhost:8983/index.html, top-level page, not the test iframe, with real clicks and keys at 1280 wide. I selected a shape, opened Colouring, clicked the Opacity box and typed 50, then clicked the selected layer on the canvas. The box was still the active element, still read "50", and fillOpacity was still 1. Space went into the box (its value became " ") and FM.playing stayed false. Clicking the timeline afterwards moved focus to BODY, so the canvas is the surface that holds on to focus, as the hunter says. The code path matches: startMove in js/canvas-edit.js calls e.preventDefault() on pointerdown in every branch (camera pan, the selected-layer move, the nothing-selected viewpan). In Chrome, cancelling pointerdown also stops the mousedown default, so focus never leaves the input. No canvas handler blurs the focused element (grep for blur() and activeElement found none). The rangeRow value box applies only on 'change' or on Enter (js/inspector.js:232-239). The editor keydown in js/app.js:8218 sets inEdit for an INPUT target and returns early for Space, undo, delete and the other shortcuts. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this behaviour. This is not a test artefact: real input, top-level page, a step anyone takes on PC. One caveat on severity: the typed value is not lost for good. It lands as soon as he clicks something that does take focus, such as the timeline, or presses Enter. The real harm is that the canvas looks unchanged and his next keys (Space, Delete/Backspace, arrows, Cmd+Z) go into the box. I would call it medium rather than high. I did not check Safari or Firefox; the evidence is Chrome only.

all.title: Cmd+Z while drawing makes the last stroke vanish, but the next stroke brings it back (further presses undo work from before the drawing)
all.see: Drawing a sketch on PC, he presses Cmd+Z to take back a bad stroke. It disappears from the canvas, so it looks like it worked. The drawing bar's own ↶ still thinks the stroke is there, and his next stroke puts it back: the finished sketch has 3 strokes where he kept 2. Pressing Cmd+Z a few more times goes past the sketch and undoes things he did before he opened the pencil, behind the drawing. Checked by hand, not in the test: three presses removed the whole Sketch layer, and the tool then started a new sketch holding only the next stroke.
all.test: HUNT-c Cmd+Z while drawing takes back the last stroke, and his next stroke does not bring it back — fails with: drawing on PC, he pressed Cmd+Z to take back his second stroke — it vanished from the canvas, but Cmd+Z did not take the stroke back in the drawing tool (it still held 2 strokes while the canvas showed 1); his next stroke brought the undone one back: the finished sketch has 3 strokes where he kept 2.
all.evidence: js/app.js:8262 `if (mod && (e.key === 'z' || e.key === 'Z')) { … FM.history.undo() }` runs whatever tool is on screen. The drawing tool keeps its own stroke list and undo stack (sessionSubs / histPast, js/draw-tool.js undoStep ~549, exposed as FM.drawTool._undo). Each stroke commits to the app history (js/draw-tool.js ~357 FM.history.commit()). history.restore's afterExternalChange resyncs the mask tool (js/history.js:153) and the group view, but never the drawing tool. So the next commitStroke re-fits the layer from the stale sessionSubs. The draw tool's own capture keydown (js/draw-tool.js:1054) only takes Enter and Escape.
all.fix: While FM.drawTool.active, send Cmd/Ctrl+Z to FM.drawTool._undo() and Cmd+Shift+Z / Cmd+Y to _redo(), in the draw tool's capture keydown or at the top of app.js's undo branch, with preventDefault. The other editor shortcuts (Tab, Space, digits, A/S/D, Delete) should not reach the project while drawing either.

verdict.reason:
I reran it on the worktree's server (port 8983, which was already serving hunt6-c) and it fails the same way: after Cmd+Z the drawing tool still holds 2 strokes while the canvas shows 1, and the finished sketch ends up with 3 strokes instead of 2.

The code backs this up. The drawing tool's own keydown handler (js/draw-tool.js:1054, capture phase) only takes Enter and Escape, so Cmd+Z falls through to the app's keydown (js/app.js:8262). There, nothing checks FM.drawTool.active, and the key goes straight to FM.history.undo(). The overlayOwnsScreen() guard does not stop it, because the draw overlay sits inside the canvas area and does not cover the screen, and inEdit is false because focus is on the page. Every stroke after the first commits an app history step (draw-tool.js:357, from the #684 fix), so one undo puts back the scene as it was before the last stroke. history.js afterExternalChange resyncs the mask tool but never touches the drawing tool's sessionSubs, histPast or sessionLayerId. The next stroke's commitStroke then finds the same layer id and refits it from the old 3-stroke list, so the undone stroke comes back. Undoing past the first stroke deletes the layer; sessionLayerId then points at nothing and the next stroke makes a new Sketch holding only that stroke.

The test is realistic. It uses trusted CDP mouse strokes, checked by a control on isTrusted, and a trusted Cmd+Z with Meta held. Sketching is opened through the Add menu's own instant() entry, in the PC layout. Cmd+Z reaching the page on a Mac is the same path the app's normal undo already relies on. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for Cmd+Z during drawing to undo at project level. The only intended undo while drawing is the bar's own undo/redo (#165), and the transport undo is hidden while drawing (body.drawing #timeline-panel display:none), so the keyboard is the only way into this path and it is clearly unintended.

One test artefact that does not affect the verdict: pcScene690c replaces FM.scene without committing it, so going further back than one undo in the test would hit history left over from earlier tests. The test only asserts what happens after a single undo, and that part is sound.

Scope: PC or Mac with a keyboard only. A phone has no Cmd+Z. Pressing Cmd+Z to take back a stroke is an ordinary habit, and the failure is misleading: the canvas looks correct right after the undo and the stroke only comes back on the next one. Worth fixing as the report says: while drawing, send Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z to the drawing tool's own undo and redo, and keep the other editor shortcuts from reaching the project.

all.title: A sideways trackpad swipe over the preview zooms it out, and with the camera selected zooms the camera out and saves it
all.see: On his Mac trackpad, a two-finger swipe sideways over the preview (no up or down movement at all) shrinks the preview away from him: 12 small events took it to 0.40x. With the camera selected, the same swipe zooms the camera out from 1 to 0.32 and shifts it 348px. It is keyed at the playhead and committed to undo, so his project changes from a gesture that has nothing to do with zoom. Any two-finger scroll or pinch over the preview is also far too jumpy (checked in code, not in the test): the zoom takes a fixed 8% step, or 10% on the camera, per event, whatever the size of the movement.
all.test: HUNT-c a sideways two-finger swipe on the trackpad over the preview leaves the view, and a selected camera, where they were — fails with: a sideways two-finger swipe over the preview, with no up or down in it at all: with nothing selected the preview zoomed OUT to 0.40x; with the camera selected the camera zoomed from 1 to 0.319 (x 0 to 348) and it is saved in his project — every sideways wheel event counts as a zoom-out step.
all.evidence: js/canvas-edit.js:725 `s1 = … s0 * (e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.08 : 1 / 1.08)` and js/canvas-edit.js:739 `nz = … zoom * (e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 1 / 1.1)`, followed by FM.setTransform on the camera's x, y and scale and a delayed history.commit. deltaY === 0 falls into the zoom-out arm, and the event's size is ignored. Control inside the test: one real 100px notch up over the preview zooms it in, so the wheel reaches this handler. The Add-menu pager (js/addmenu.js ~1544) already ignores sideways and repeated deltas, which is the right pattern.
all.fix: In onWheel, return without preventDefault when deltaY is 0 or |deltaX| > |deltaY|. Scale the zoom by the event's size, e.g. factor = Math.exp(-clamp(deltaY, -50, 50) / 100), so a trackpad scroll or pinch moves smoothly and a mouse notch still steps.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test and it fails the same way. I served the hunt6-c worktree on port 8983. An existing server from the same worktree was already on that port, so mine exited with "address in use", and I confirmed the running one's cwd is hunt6-c. Result: with nothing selected the preview went to 0.40x, and with the camera selected the camera scale went from 1 to 0.319 and x from 0 to 348. The test is sound. It sends trusted CDP wheel events (the listener confirms isTrusted), and it has a working control: one real notch up over the preview zooms it in, so the handler under test is the one that receives the events.

The code confirms the cause. onWheel in js/canvas-edit.js is attached to the canvas at line 1001. It picks the direction with `e.deltaY < 0 ? zoom-in : zoom-out`, at line 725 for the view and line 739 for the camera. It never looks at deltaX, and it calls preventDefault in both branches. So any event with deltaY of 0 counts as a zoom-out step. Real hardware produces these: a sideways two-finger swipe on a Mac trackpad, a horizontal thumb-wheel, or Shift+wheel. The same happens with a mostly-sideways swipe whose small up-down jitter is 0 or positive, so it drifts toward zoom-out.

With nothing selected this is view-only: annoying, but his project does not change. With the camera selected it writes x, y and scale keyframes at the playhead and saves them to undo about 400ms later, so his project really changes. That is a user-facing defect.

It is not behaviour he asked for. REQUESTS.md and the code comment ("pinch/wheel zooms") only say the up-down wheel zooms. Nothing says a sideways scroll should zoom, and searching REQUESTS.md for wheel with preview, canvas, camera or zoom turns up nothing that contradicts this.

One caveat: the report's second claim, that two-finger scrolls and pinches are too jumpy because every event is a fixed 8% (camera: 10%) step, is only checked by reading the code. This test does not measure it. It is plausible from lines 725 and 739, but unproven here.

confirmed.title: After sharing stops, undo takes back a change from the session instead of the one he just made
confirmed.see: He taps Stop sharing on the Mac and keeps working on his project. He renames a layer and presses Undo. The rename he just made stays. Instead, a rename he made earlier, during the session, quietly reverts. Pressing Undo again does nothing, so his latest change cannot be undone until he opens another project. The phone gets the same thing after the owner ends the session: the friend's latest edit to their copy cannot be undone, and Undo reverts one of their session edits instead.
confirmed.test: HUNT-d after he stops sharing, undo takes back an edit from the session instead of the one he just made — on his Mac and on the phone that was in it.
